 Emma Raducanu swaps tennis court for Lake District adventure

 Tennis star Emma Raducanu has swapped the court for the Cumbrian countryside during a trip to the Lake District.
 The former US Open champion shared a series of pictures from her visit with her millions of followers on Instagram.
 Captioning the post “Timeout in the Lakes”, the 23-year-old showed fans how she had been spending some downtime away from tennis.
 Her Lake District break included a visit to Graythwaite Adventure, where Raducanu tried her hand at shooting.
 The attraction, based on the Graythwaite Estate in the southern Lake District, offers a range of outdoor experiences amid the Cumbrian landscape.
 Raducanu became one of the biggest names in British sport after her remarkable victory at the US Open in 2021.
 Then aged just 18, she came through qualifying before going on to win the women's singles title without dropping a set during the tournament.
 The achievement made her the first qualifier in the Open Era to win a Grand Slam singles title.
 Her latest visit puts Cumbria in front of a sizeable international audience, with Raducanu's Instagram account attracting millions of followers.
 The trip comes during time away from competitive tennis for the British star, who has faced injury problems during the 2026 season.
 Her Lake District photographs offered followers a glimpse of how she has been spending some of that time away, with the tennis star summing up her Cumbrian getaway simply as: “Timeout in the Lakes.”
